decisions.head: artisanal
decisions.reason: Direct current English Wiktionary food/item sense verifies skilled artisan production. Preserve the item/food qualifier; no invented superior-quality or homemade equivalence.

decisions.head: doppelgänger
decisions.reason: The direct English entry verifies the accented alternative spelling, resolving the stale empty extract. Select the similar-double sense rather than a ghost or fictional monster.

explain.head: doppelganger
explain.reason: The explicit spelling pointer leads to the remarkably similar double sense appropriate to the twin anchor, without claiming biological kinship.

decisions.head: soirée
decisions.reason: Restore the historical accent loss while retaining the stable ID. Direct English source verifies the alternative form and the base source explains a formal evening party.

explain.head: soiree
explain.reason: Exact alternative spelling resolves to the evening-party noun, not the French general evening sense.

decisions.head: wintertide
decisions.reason: Direct English source verifies a literary/archaic winter-time noun. Preserve both register labels so learners are not taught it as the ordinary everyday replacement for winter.

explain.head: wintertime
explain.reason: The explicit source pointer denotes the season between autumn and spring. No literary quotations or unsourced example is imported.

decisions.head: realignment
decisions.reason: Explain the action noun through realign and the organizational sense of align, appropriate to reorganization; physical-line and genetic alignments are not selected.

explain.head: realign
explain.reason: The noun explicitly invokes realigning; retain again/anew without inventing a political-party interpretation.

explain.head: align
explain.reason: Use organize-consistently to resolve the intermediate verb in the business context, not DNA alignment.

decisions.head: reintegration
decisions.reason: Explain the process of integrating again using the constituent-part sense. No unsupported historical Reconstruction or specific rehabilitation result is asserted.

explain.head: reintegrate
explain.reason: Explicitly named repeated integration supplies the first step of the source-grounded chain.

explain.head: integrate
explain.reason: Including as a constituent part explains integration generally in organizational/academic contexts, not calculus.

decisions.head: catalyzer
decisions.reason: Select the general chemical-reaction agent, not the catalytic converter; clarify catalyze and catalysis while retaining US/Canada labels. No claim that all catalysts are enzymes.

explain.head: catalyze
explain.reason: The agent noun explicitly refers to catalyzing; select the chemical reaction rather than the figurative inspiration sense.

explain.head: catalysis
explain.reason: The reaction-acceleration definition explains the intermediate technical term, with chemical material unchanged at reaction end.

decisions.head: sanitizer
decisions.reason: The explicit agent noun is now explained by the cleaning/disinfecting verb sense, not the compiler or document-censorship meanings. No product efficacy percentage or health advice is added.

explain.head: sanitize
explain.reason: The noun explicitly derives from sanitize; select the microorganisms/cleaning sense relevant to cleaner.

decisions.head: semidiameter
decisions.reason: Reviewed hyphen-only correction with stable identity. Publish only the source's apparent astronomical radius sense; do not label it a universal synonym for every physical radius.

decisions.head: cubic decimeter
decisions.reason: Exact US-spelling source points to the modern cubic-volume definition, replacing the selected outdated water-volume evidence while preserving it hidden. Stable ID and US label remain.

explain.head: cubic decimetre
explain.reason: Explicit US-to-UK spelling relation supports the same unit: a decimetre-sided cube, one litre. Preserve the spelling-region labels in the base explanation.

decisions.head: mol
decisions.reason: Direct English source identifies a dated chemistry/physics spelling of mole. Expand with the modern amount-of-substance definition, not molecular weight expressed in grams.

explain.head: mole
explain.reason: Exact chemistry/physics unit sense with the defined entity count; exclude animal, spy, skin and other homonyms.

decisions.head: gram molecule
decisions.reason: Reviewed hyphen-to-space correction preserves letters and stable ID. The source explicitly defines a mole of molecules; clarify amount of substance with the current unit definition.

explain.head: mole
explain.reason: The source names a mole of molecules; retain the entity-count unit definition instead of the older mass-only WordNet candidate.
